purpose: Carry the live, append-only, role-scoped execution and access state for the parser-v3-v2 set-repair lifecycle, so that the FINAL Phase 1.2G acceptance policy never has to be edited to record that something happened.

policy_binding.bytes_modified_note: One block changed: review_provenance. Audit A and Audit B were listed without finding counts while C, D and E carried them, and the limitation asserted that the Audit E remediation had not been re-reviewed, which Phase 1.2H made false by re-reviewing it. No threshold, gate, population figure, ontology entry, comparator role, status rule or execution_state value was touched.
policy_binding.note: policy_semantics_sha256 is computed over the policy with the five mutable execution_state counters listed in semantic_projection_counter_excludes projected out, and nothing else. It is the load-bearing binding: it stays stable across any future licensed counter increment, so a change to a threshold, gate, ontology entry, population figure, comparator role, status rule or execution-state prose cannot hide behind a routine state update. Audit G rejected the earlier design, which projected out the whole execution_state block: excluding a container also excludes the free text inside it, and that text could then be rewritten to assert a completed evaluation without moving the hash.

phase_1_2g_finalization_snapshot.role: Immutable snapshot of the execution_state block as the Phase 1.2G policy finalized it. It is history, not live state; live state is live_counters below.

values.final_policy_is_not_a_result: status=FINAL records that the rule for judging a future evaluation is settled. It records nothing about any parser. Parser v3 remains unvalidated, parser-v3-v1 remains SEALED / UNSPENT / UNSCORABLE / RETIRED_AS_INELIGIBLE, no set exists for parser-v3-v2, and no evaluation has been run.

counter_semantics.retired_v1_repair_access: Access to the retired parser-v3-v1 sealed set for repair purposes only. A semantic read decodes case content; a byte-only integrity verification streams bytes to a digest and discards them. They are counted separately because only the first changes what a human has seen.
counter_semantics.formal_v2_evaluation_access: Access to a future sealed parser-v3-v2 set for formal evaluation. Distinct from repair access: a repair read must never be reported as, or aggregated with, an evaluation read.
counter_semantics.v2_construction: Construction, sealing, listing-witness and final-contract activity for the successor set.
counter_semantics.parser_execution: Parser invocations and prediction generation. Must remain zero for the whole of Phase 1.2H.
counter_semantics.azure: Control-plane reads are configuration and existence queries. Data-plane content reads and writes are object access. They are separate because a reachability probe is not a data access. See counter_provenance: the two data-plane counters come from the execution receipt and job_executions from Azure's own execution list. Independent Audit F (F-01) found this sentence calling the receipt SIGNED. It is not signed. Nothing signs it and nothing verifies a signature; it is a JSON document the probe wrote about itself, and its authority is that of a self-report. What is independently observed is the platform execution list, which records that the execution the receipt names exists, succeeded, and ran the image digest the receipt claims -- scripts/phase1_2h_r1_review_boundary_assessment.py assert_execution_is_platform_attested enforces exactly that binding. So 'exact' here means 'transcribed from a named field without rounding', not 'independently attested'; control_plane_reads and resource_creations_or_changes are operator-maintained and are not load-bearing safety counters.

counter_provenance.role: Distinguishes counters derived from machine evidence from counters an operator maintains by hand, and distinguishes both from counters whose value is a property of the source rather than a measurement of a run. Audit-relevant because a hand-maintained number must never be presented with the authority of a receipt-derived one, and because a literal the emitting program writes is not the same kind of fact as a value read back from a machine artifact.

receipt_derived_exact.evidence: Each value appears as a named field of docs/phase1_2h_r1_access_receipt_003.json, which is committed and validated against docs/phase1_2h_r1_access_receipt.schema.json by scripts/phase1_2h_r1_receipt_validator.py. The mapping is: azure.data_plane_content_reads <- counters.azure_data_plane_content_reads; azure.data_plane_writes <- counters.azure_data_plane_writes; sealed_input_semantic_reads <- counters.semantic_input_reads; sealed_label_semantic_reads <- counters.semantic_label_reads; parser_invocations_on_private_or_locked_data <- counters.parser_invocations; candidate_predictions_generated <- counters.predictions_generated.
receipt_derived_exact.note: Audit C (C-02) found byte_only_integrity_verifications: 14 presented here as though the receipt reported it, when the receipt reports 12. Audit F (F-06) then found the added note insufficient: a composite left inside this class still borrows its authority, because a reader who checks the class contract rather than the note is told the value was copied from a receipt field. The counter has been moved to composite_of_separately_evidenced_parts, which requires it to decompose and which the validator enforces. Every counter remaining in this class is a single receipt field.

azure_verified_exact.evidence: docs/phase1_2h_r1_job_execution_inventory.json is the committed output of the control-plane execution list for the access-gate job. It records exactly two platform executions: dlv8kmc, which the probe's own environment check refused, and 0fqre0m, the passing gate. Audit C (C-13) found this counter previously cited only an uncommitted command, so the inventory was captured and committed.
azure_verified_exact.note: The inventory also resolves the gap Audit C noticed between the operator's attempt numbering, which reaches 003, and the two executions that exist: attempt 002 was prepared but never started and produced no execution. See operator_attempt_numbering in that file.

structurally_zero_by_source_analysis.evidence: These are zero because no first-party code path that could make them non-zero exists, checked by AST over the two files listed in IN_JOB_FIRST_PARTY_SOURCES in scripts/phase1_2h_r1_private_source_probe.py (the probe itself and scripts/phase1_2h_r1_receipt_validator.py): assert_no_write_calls_in_first_party_source refuses any mutating Blob call, and assert_byte_handling_is_digest_only refuses any use of an object-byte chunk other than as an argument to a SHA-256 digest, with global, nonlocal, assignment, return and re-iteration of that name all refused. Audit E (E-05) found the earlier wording claiming AST enforcement for counters that no AST check touches; those have been moved to zero_because_the_activity_has_never_occurred, and what remains here is only what the checks actually reach. The scope is first-party source: the Azure SDK, the standard library and the base image are not parsed, and nothing is claimed about them.
structurally_zero_by_source_analysis.note: private_curator_files_read is additionally zero because the probe's blob enumeration is bound to the frozen prefix and member list in docs/phase1_2h_r1_access_decision_record.json, which contains no curator file; command line and environment cannot redirect it. Where a zero rests only on source analysis that is the whole of its basis and it is stated as such.

operator_maintained_approximate.evidence: None. These are hand-maintained counts kept across an interactive round and no machine artifact establishes them.
operator_maintained_approximate.note: They are recorded because a round that provisioned Azure resources must say so, not because any safety property depends on their exact value. resource_creations_or_changes enumerates: the user-assigned identity, its two role assignments, three image pushes, the job creation and two job updates. control_plane_reads is an order-of-magnitude count of az configuration and existence queries and must not be cited as a precise measurement. No safety counter may be classified here; validate_ledger() enforces that.

composite_of_separately_evidenced_parts.evidence: The value 14 is a sum of two observations with different provenance and no single class describes it honestly. 12 come from docs/phase1_2h_r1_access_receipt_003.json field counters.byte_only_integrity_verifications, one per authoritative sealed object streamed by the Phase 1.2H-R1 gate; that receipt is committed and schema-validated. 2 are carried forward from event 2 of this ledger, where two local curator files were verified by digest before R1 existed; those predate any receipt and rest on the committed ledger event alone.

retired_v1_repair_access.byte_only_integ.note: One per authoritative sealed object streamed to SHA-256 by the in-VNet access-gate job.

retired_v1_repair_access.byte_only_integ.evidence: Event 2 of this ledger, docs/phase1_2h_execution_access_ledger.json; no execution receipt exists for these.
retired_v1_repair_access.byte_only_integ.note: Pre-R1 local curator-file digest verifications over different files, retained because removing them would understate what has been verified.

composite_of_separately_evidenced_parts.note: Introduced for Audit F (F-06). The class exists so that a counter summing differently evidenced addends cannot be labelled with the strongest of them.

zero_because_the_activity_has_never_occu.evidence: No formal parser-v3 evaluation has ever been run, no parser-v3-v2 set exists, and no comparator has been executed against locked inputs. Two committed artifacts establish this rather than one. (1) The state blocks of this file, docs/phase1_2h_execution_access_ledger.json: retired_v1_state has formal_evaluation_ever_run false and prediction_streams_generated_against_v1 false, and successor_set_state records that no successor set has been constructed or sealed. (2) Those blocks are not free text. src/jspace_observation/parser_v3_v2_access_ledger.py refuses to validate any ledger in which formal_evaluation_ever_run is true or prediction_streams_generated_against_v1 is true, in _validate_retired_v1_state, so the assertion cannot be flipped by editing this file: it would have to be flipped in the validator, in a reviewed commit, alongside the evaluation artifacts that do not exist.
zero_because_the_activity_has_never_occu.note: Introduced for Audit E (E-05). These zeros were previously classified as structurally zero by source analysis, which was not true of them: no AST check in this repository examines a scoring path or a comparator run, because no such code was written. The honest basis is that the activity never happened, which is a weaker fact and is now labelled as one. It is still machine evidence in the sense the ledger requires -- a committed state block, not a recollection -- but it would stop being true the moment such a round were authorized, whereas a source-analysis zero would not.

events.summary: Verified HEAD == origin/main == 0480f4fae869090d8bd2abc72373e9a0e1dd3e49, clean worktree, focused suite 446 passed, full suite 1821 passed.

Streamed the two local retired-v1 curator files to SHA-256 and compared digest and byte count against the committed public set manifest. Both matched. Bytes were discarded; no record was decoded, parsed, printed or retained.

Resolved the registered authoritative sealed source from committed evidence and probed reachability at the control plane and at the container metadata layer only. The storage account reports publicNetworkAccess=Disabled and the data plane refused the request under its network rules. The registered set prefix was never listed and no object was requested.

The authoritative retired-v1 source cannot be authenticated or read with the required read-only boundary from this environment, so the local curator copy may not be substituted for it. Round terminated BLOCKED_ON_PRIVATE_SOURCE_ACCESS before any private access.

Phase 1.2H-R1. Event 3 concluded the data plane was unreachable; the correct reading was that it was unreachable from OUTSIDE the virtual network, which is what publicNetworkAccess=Disabled means. Provisioned an in-VNet execution boundary instead: a user-assigned identity holding exactly two role assignments (Storage Blob Data Reader scoped to the single container, AcrPull scoped to the registry), a pinned-digest image, and a Container Apps job on the workload-profiles environment attached to the private-endpoint subnet. No role granting write, delete, delegation or role-assignment-read was requested at any point.

R1 execution 001 (job execution dlv8kmc) refused before authenticating and exited non-zero. The probe's own forbidden-environment denylist named MSI_ENDPOINT and MSI_SECRET, which are exactly how Container Apps supplies the managed identity the protocol requires, so the rule was self-contradictory. The refusal is recorded because it is evidence the pre-flight guard fires on the operator's own error, not only on a hypothetical one. No listing and no object request occurred.

R1 execution 003 (job execution 0fqre0m, image sha256:f2cf1701aab098236b5ce850f11b218f723dc7a9c2dd01cc8853e7572022ee15) passed the byte-only access gate. One list operation over the exact registered prefix returned 12 members equal as a set to the committed public manifest; each object was streamed to SHA-256 in chunks and discarded; 396613 bytes total; every per-object digest and size matched; the aggregate digest reproduced the committed public anchor e1364afcac87516813d33a4e9fb3e370769487ab2f3ca47a08a3b4059db14e71. decode_attempts=0, persist_attempts=0, data_plane_writes=0, semantic_input_reads=0, semantic_label_reads=0, parser_invocations=0, predictions_generated=0. Twelve invariants checked, none failed. The receipt is committed at docs/phase1_2h_r1_access_receipt_003.json and is content-free by construction: it carries digests, counts and booleans only.

Supersedes the event-4 determination for Phase 1.2H-R1 only; event 4 remains the accurate record of the earlier round. Authenticated byte-only access to the authoritative source is now established, so BLOCKED_ON_PRIVATE_SOURCE_ACCESS no longer describes the blocker. The blocker has moved: repair requires a semantic read, a semantic read requires a private review boundary, and the executable boundary assessment scored 0 of 13 conditions passed, 5 failed and 8 not assessable, verdict DOES_NOT_QUALIFY. No qualifying private semantic-review backend exists in the subscription: the resource group contains zero Microsoft.CognitiveServices accounts and zero ML workspaces, and the worker subnet has no egress control (routeTable=null, natGateway=null, no custom outbound NSG rule). Round terminated BLOCKED_ON_PRIVATE_REVIEW_BOUNDARY. Under protocol section 12.3 this state applies even though the byte-only gate passed.

Erratum to event 8, appended rather than substituted because recorded events are immutable. Independent Audit C found two defects in event 8's text; neither changes the round's terminal state, which remains BLOCKED_ON_PRIVATE_REVIEW_BOUNDARY, and neither changes any counter. (1) Event 8 cites 'protocol section 12.3'. No such section exists: docs/phase1_2h_r1_cloud_access_protocol.md has ten sections. The intended reference is section 10, Terminal states, read together with section 8, The private review boundary. Event 8 also states that the terminal state applies 'even though the byte-only gate passed', which the protocol table then rendered as 'regardless of byte-only outcome'. That wording was wrong in the other direction and has been corrected: the states are ordered by precedence, and BLOCKED_ON_PRIVATE_REVIEW_BOUNDARY REQUIRES a passing gate, because a round that never reached the source has not reached the boundary question. Event 8's own reasoning is consistent with that ordering; only its citation was wrong. (2) Event 8 asserts that no qualifying private semantic-review backend exists 'in the subscription'. The committed evidence does not reach that far. It covers resource group rg-jspace-observation-sea in region southeastasia: a full resource listing of that group, its network posture, and its private-endpoint inventory. The supportable claim is that no qualifying backend exists in the resource group and region in which this work runs, and none is reachable from the worker subnet under the required boundary. Whether some other resource group in the subscription holds a Cognitive Services account was not observed and is not asserted. Event 8 also omits that one candidate was found and disqualified rather than none being found at all: an Azure OpenAI-class backend could be provisioned, but the existing worker subnet snet-aca-jspace-sea-v2 has routeTable null, natGateway null and no custom outbound NSG rule, so AllowInternetOutBound at priority 65001 applies and unrestricted egress would accompany any private material the worker held. Two of the thirteen frozen conditions fail on that ground alone. The boundary therefore fails on egress control as well as on backend absence, and provisioning a reviewer without also constraining egress would not clear it.

retired_v1_state.repair_access_purpose: byte-only integrity verification of the authoritative sealed source; no repair read was performed and no case content was decoded
retired_v1_state.current_state_note: The Phase 1.2H state transition to REPAIR_ACCESSED did NOT occur. Phase 1.2H-R1 authenticated to the authoritative source and streamed all 12 objects, but only to a digest: no byte was decoded, retained or interpreted, so nothing about any case is known that was not already public. UNSPENT therefore remains accurate without qualification, and the label is unchanged. What changed is the operator's ability to reach the source, not the state of the set.

successor_set_state.sealed_object_count_note: null, not zero. Under limitation L-32 a sealed member list and sealed_object_count require an authenticated seal-time observation. No set was sealed, so the quantity is undefined rather than measured to be zero, and an offline assertion must not stand in for the observation.
